dataset.title: NJ School Performance Reports
dataset.publisher: NJ Dept. of Education, Office of Performance Reports
dataset.subject: https://www.nj.gov/education/spr/
dataset.pitfall: NJ publishes two 4-year graduation rates; only the State calculation has a multi-year trend — plotting the Federal rate as a trend (it has one point) is the classic misread.
unknowns: Pre-2015-16 editions have not been examined; the format eras before that are unknown to us.
We do not track which NJSLA cut scores changed between editions.

coverage.entities: every NJ public school, district, and the state

issues.title: Files live under /education/sprreports/, not the /education/spr/ landing path
issues.detection: 404s when constructing file URLs from the landing-page path

issues.title: Code columns typed 'Numeric' in the layout are zero-padded TEXT in the data
issues.detection: CountyCode='13', DistrictCode='4900' — string cells with leading zeros preserved
issues.misuse: Coercing codes to integers strips leading zeros and silently breaks the warehouse join.

issues.title: Rate cells carry % signs, prose suppression sentences, and >90%/<10% privacy caps
issues.detection: value fails float() after stripping a trailing % — includes '>90%', '<10%', and sentences like 'Fewer than 10 students were in the graduation cohort.'
issues.misuse: Treating suppression NULLs as zero. Capped extremes also go NULL — harmless for All Students, a real loss for small subgroups.
issues.instead: Leave suppressed values NULL, exclude them from denominators, and say so in captions for small subgroups.

semantic: a rate column parses as numeric for some rows and prose for others

issues.title: State and Federal 4-yr graduation rates coexist; only State is populated across years
issues.detection: 4YrGraduationRateState_District non-empty in 27,115 of 27,201 trend rows; Federal in only 5,423 (≈ one year)
issues.misuse: Drawing the Federal rate as a trend line (it has one point), or comparing a State figure against another state's federal ACGR — NJ's State calc runs higher (SOMSD 2024-25: State 93.2% vs Federal 89.4%).
issues.instead: Plot the State rate as the trend; headline the latest-year Federal ACGR beside it and caption the difference.

issues.title: District/state context blends all tested grades; a school's value covers only its own
issues.misuse: Reading a high school's math proficiency sitting below its district as a deficit — the district figure blends grades 3–8 with HS course tests over different populations.

practices.title: Use NJDOE's published school-wide proficiency; do not rebuild it from grade/test rows
practices.question: What share of this school's students met or exceeded expectations?
practices.rule: Read the school-wide MetExceed value NJDOE publishes at the school grain.
practices.naive: Averaging or summing the per-grade, per-test rows in assessment_grade up to a school figure.
practices.because: Suppressed cells drop out of a home-grown aggregate silently, and grade/course mix differs by school — one capped Algebra I cohort once inflated a school's rebuilt figure well above its published one.
practices.residual: We inherit NJDOE's own inclusions and exclusions, which are not fully documented; our figure matches the published one and is no more transparent than it.

practices.title: Report the State and Federal graduation rates as distinct measures, never combined
practices.question: What is this district's four-year graduation rate?
rule: Use the State calculation for any multi-year trend — it is the only one populated across years.
Report a Federal (ACGR) figure only as a single labelled year.
Never average, splice, or plot the two in one series.
practices.naive: Plotting whichever rate is present per year, producing one line that silently switches definitions.
practices.because: The two use different cohort rules; a spliced series shows a step change that is an artifact of the definition, not of any school's performance.
practices.because_not: We considered publishing only the Federal rate for cross-state comparability and rejected it: with one populated year it answers almost no question a reader actually asks about NJ.

validations.method: confirmed from real data — 2024-25 District/State file
validations.result: codes are zero-padded TEXT; All-Students label is 'All Students'; suppression is prose sentences; SchoolYear format matches warehouse

changes.note: Page created in ergo format; 5 issues registered from the 2024-25 acquisition notes.

prose.url-host-split:
The landing page is a JS app whose `download.js` builds the real links:
`https://www.nj.gov/education/sprreports/download/DataFiles/<YEAR>/<file>`
with hyphenated years (`2024-2025`). Easy to fetch the wrong path.
prose.layout-types-lie:
Confirmed against the 2024-25 District/State file: the data cells match the
warehouse's TEXT keys verbatim, so the *correct* behavior is to trust the
data over the data dictionary.
prose.rate-prose-suppression:
Parse rule: a value is a number iff it parses after stripping a trailing
`%`; everything else → NULL. Four distinct suppression sentences observed in
the 2024-25 files, plus the two extreme caps.
prose.grad-state-vs-federal:
The trajectory uses the State calculation; the latest-year Federal ACGR is
headlined where present, with the difference noted in the caption.
prose.grade-mix-context:
Real, not a bug: comparisons across aggregation levels compare different
grade mixes. Per-grade views (`assessment_grade`) are the honest grain.
prose.headline-proficiency-as-published:
The reader-facing number on NJDOE's own report card is the published one.
Any figure we compute that disagrees with it will be read as an error in our
work, and usually is.
prose.grad-calcs-stay-separate:
Cross-state comparison is the one job the Federal rate does better, and it
is worth saying out loud that another newsroom covering multiple states
might reasonably invert this call.

lede:
Worked example of an ergo data page, condensed from the real page in
[njschooldata](https://github.com/lavallee/njschooldata). New Jersey's
official annual "report card" for every public school and district —
assessments, graduation, absenteeism, growth — and the authoritative source
for academic-outcome reporting.
